Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

occupy verb

keep busy; take up time

also busy, be busy, keep busy, occupied, be occupied with, keep someone occupied, take up (time)

classical

Cic. Sen. 32: nēmō … cui fuerim occupātus
Cic. Off. 1.57: in patriā dēlendā occupātī (Lewis & Short)

occupātus, occupāta, occupātum

adjective (participle of occupō); with in + ablative

busy, occupied, engaged

Busy with something is in aliquā rē occupātus. The opposite is ōtiōsus, at leisure (Cic. Tusc. 1.5); for “free, not busy” see available.

Other words

  • occupō, occupāre, occupāvī, occupātum — take up, occupy (time, a person)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8.10.3: haec causa prīmōs mēnsēs occupābit (Lewis & Short)

    Of a task that takes up time or attention; its first sense is to seize (see occupy-seize).

  • dētineō, dētinēre, dētinuī, dētentum — keep busy, engage; detain

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.132: in aliēnīs negōtiīs dētinērī (Lewis & Short)

    Properly to hold back or detain; then to keep someone occupied.

  • negōtiōsus, negōtiōsa, negōtiōsum — busy, full of business

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 8.5 (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Merc. 1.2.79; Traupman 285

    Busy with affairs and work; also of a thing that gives much work (prōvincia negōtiōsa, Cic. Mur. 18).

Examples

  • itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus

    and so far no one has wanted to see me and found me busyCic. Sen. 32

  • Nihil mē interpellāstī, nōn enim occupātus eram.

    You didn’t interrupt me at all: I wasn’t busy.Cord. Coll. 3.31

See also occupy, available.
